Check that a precision matrix is the maximum-likelihood network on a graph

Source: R/glasso.R
ggm_support_kkt.Rd

ggm_support_kkt() checks whether a precision matrix is the maximum-likelihood Gaussian graphical model on a given graph, for the correlation or covariance matrix it was fitted to. Some Gaussian graphical models are estimated without a penalty: a graph is chosen first, and the precision matrix is then the maximum-likelihood estimate under the constraint that every pair of variables not joined by an edge has a partial correlation of zero.

This constrained estimate is unique and is characterized by two conditions: the covariance implied by the model reproduces the observed covariance for every pair joined by an edge and for every variance, and the precision matrix is zero for every pair that is not joined. A matrix meeting both conditions is the maximum-likelihood network on that graph.

ggm_support_kkt() returns the largest violation of these conditions; a value near zero shows that the matrix is the constrained optimum, up to numerical precision.

Networks from ggm_modselect(), logo_network() and ebic_glasso(refit = "unregularized") store this value, and certificate() reports it. Penalized graphical lasso networks are checked by glasso_kkt().

Usage

ggm_support_kkt(theta, cor_matrix, support, active_tol = 1e-08)

Arguments

theta

The precision matrix to check: a finite, square numeric matrix.

cor_matrix

The correlation or covariance matrix the model was fitted to, of the same size as theta.

support

A logical matrix of the same size, TRUE where an edge is allowed, with no missing values. It is made symmetric, so an upper- or lower-triangular matrix describes the same graph; the diagonal is ignored.

active_tol

A single finite number >= 0 (default 1e-8). It is checked but does not affect the result: every entry of theta outside the graph counts as a violation of its absolute size.

Value

A single number, the largest absolute violation of the conditions: 0 at the exact constrained optimum, Inf for an asymmetric or non-positive-definite theta.

Details

For a Gaussian graphical model on a graph \(G\), with \(W = \Theta^{-1}\), the maximum-likelihood conditions are \(W_{ij} = S_{ij}\) for every \((i,j)\) in \(G\) and on the diagonal, and \(\Theta_{ij} = 0\) for every \((i,j)\) not in \(G\). The function returns the largest absolute deviation from these conditions; a theta that is asymmetric (by more than 1e-8) or not positive definite returns Inf.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when theta is not a finite square numeric matrix, cor_matrix is not a finite matrix of the same size, support is not a logical matrix of that size without missing values, or active_tol is not a single finite number >= 0.

See also

certificate(), which reports the stored value of a fitted network; ggm_modselect() and logo_network(); glasso_kkt() for penalized networks.

Examples

S <- 0.4^abs(outer(1:6, 1:6, "-"))
# An AR(1) correlation has a tridiagonal inverse: the chain graph is exact.
chain <- abs(row(S) - col(S)) <= 1
ggm_support_kkt(solve(S), S, support = chain)
#> [1] 2.220446e-16
# The same precision violates an empty-graph (diagonal) constraint.
ggm_support_kkt(solve(S), S, support = diag(6) > 0)
#> [1] 0.4761905
# A fitted network reports its value through certificate().
certificate(ggm_modselect(cor_matrix = S, n = 250))
#>   method  certificate kind certified
#> 1    ggm 2.220446e-16  kkt      TRUE
